newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Latvia urges Baltic customs union on way to EU.
newsitem.headline: Latvia urges Baltic customs union on way to EU.

text.p: The prime minister of the Baltic state of Latvia on Saturday urged the formation of a customs union to link the three small Baltic nations, saying it would help them on the road to the European Union (EU).

Latvian Prime Minister Andris Shkele, Lithuanian Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius and Estonian premier Mart Simann met in the Estonian coastal town of Parnu and trade issues were high on the agenda.
The three Baltic states, which quit the former Soviet Union in 1991 and are trying hard to reforge links with the West, are seen as a common trade area by many foreign investors.
But businessmen often complain that moving goods across these countries with a combined population of eight million people is unnecessarily complicated and expensive.
"The formation of a Baltic customs union is one of our current tasks," Shkele said in a speech.

"A Baltic customs union according to EU principles -- the free movement of goods, services, capital and people -- will facilitate the formation of a united Baltic market as well as ease the entry of the Baltic states into the EU," he added.

The Balts are eager for EU entry and have all signed association agreements with the trading bloc. All expect to start admission talks after a summit in June which is expected to pave the way for EU enlargement.
The other leaders also dealt with trade and Estonia's Siimann said hidden barriers to free trade would be pulled down by the end of this year, the Baltic News Service quoted him as saying.
